newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai opens first Western-style shopping mall.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai opens first Western-style shopping mall.

text.p: Shanghai's first international-style shopping mall opened in the city's bustling Nanjing Road on Friday, with 70 stores selling everything from clothes to food and jewellery.

The 11-story Meilongzheng Plaza, with floor space of 70,000 square metres (753,473 sq ft), was jointly owned by the Meilongzheng Group, and Hong Kong's Hutchison Whampoa Property Ltd, Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd, and Tem Fat Hing Fung (Holdings) Ltd, the Business News said.
Total investment in the plaza was $230 million, a Meilongzheng sales executive told Reuters. He declined to give further details.
Japanese department stores Isetan and Itohkin were among the stores in the plaza, the newspaper said.

Shanghai is considered China's shopping and fashion mecca, with retail sales in the first half of 1997 hitting 65.1 billion yuan ($7.84 billion), up a year-on-year 16.5 percent, official figures show.
